audit.kind: independent audit of the existing E3 fixture family
audit.scope: fixtures/e3/cases, scripts/verify_e3_fixtures.py, tests/test_e3_fixtures.py and runtime read/write path authority

established: six exposed cases with exact schema and roles 2 train / 1 dev / 2 heldout / 1 interrupted
every case starts failing and its reference repair makes the independent evaluator pass in an isolated copy
reference repairs change only the target constant and preserve both non-target constants; destructive rewrites fail
evaluators are stdlib-only, do not execute or import workspace code, and fail closed with a unittest failure (not an ambiguous crash) on malformed workspaces
evaluator/ and case.json are outside model read/write authority; only real run_test output discloses the required bound
no expected value or reference-repair content is reachable from the prompt or workspace text
size bounds and symlink/generated-file checks hold; the validator never mutates the committed fixture family

leak_checks.cross_case_transfer: target (constant, expected) pairs are unique; no target pair assignment or expected-value token appears in another case prompt/workspace. The only overlap (dev_retry_03 target MAX_RETRIES=4 also present as a non-target in heldout_timeout_04) was removed by changing that non-target to 3.
leak_checks.evaluator_and_case_json_reachable: absent: read_file/write_file require a workspace/... model path and reject traversal/absolute paths; runtime tests cover the negative cases
leak_checks.expected_value_in_own_goal_constraints_d: absent for all six cases (validator text + numeric-token checks)
leak_checks.expected_value_source: real run_test/verify_success output only; the below-bound assertion message names the target and minimum
leak_checks.reference_repair_content_model_reachable: absent: reference_repair lives in case.json, outside model read/write authority; its content is compared against prompt and workspace text
leak_checks.unrelated_constant_values_in_evaluator: the two preserved values are hardcoded but already visible in the workspace; no new information is exposed
leak_checks.workspace_cannot_read_evaluator_during_r: evaluators never import or execute workspace code; they parse literal AST assignments, so model code cannot inspect the evaluator or exit the process

not_established: exposed development fixtures: heldout_* cases live on disk and are only role-labelled; there is no sealed holdout
no generalization or learned-benefit claim: six small fixture cases and role labels cannot establish transfer, capability promotion or statistical superiority
no native MPS execution validated these fixtures end-to-end in this audit; no model was loaded and no native task episode was run
residual_risks: the fixture family is exposed on disk; a training pipeline could read any case, so heldout labels do not create a sealed evaluation set

scripts/run_e3_task.py and scripts/run_e3_qualification.py can operate on case directories directly; native runs must use a host-owned copy or workspace edits and .host_tmp scratch can appear under fixtures/e3/cases. The validator ignores empty .host_tmp scratch and hashes only fixture source files; the report excludes scratch.
the bound is disclosed by the evaluator assertion message through real run_test output; a model can still decline to run the test or guess below/above the floor
small numeric separations (for example 1 vs 4 and 3 vs 8) leave little room to distinguish reasoning from guessing
runtime path normalization and the model-facing workspace/... contract are owned by RuntimeComplete; this audit exercises the current working tree but not native runs
